notes:
- Channels by name. When a person names a channel or creator ('his latest video', 'her newest short', 'their last stream'), the assistant now finds the channel itself and reads its own tabs — Videos, Shorts, Live — newest first, the same as opening the channel in YouTube. The preview names the channel it came from. No handle or link needed, and 'the latest' is the tab's first entry, not a guess from a mixed search page.
- Livestreams no longer bury regular videos in search. The results page's own marks (a LIVE badge, a 'Streamed …' line, the age, the length) are read now: a livestream or a marathon stream recording sinks below the regular videos, and a 'latest' ask picks the newest regular one. A stream still wins when the person actually asked for a live or long one, and a preview that is a livestream says so.
- Voice notes are read every time, not sometimes. Three causes of the misses are closed: a sound that arrives in ranged pieces with no usable size header was sometimes handed to the AI as a fragment (which it refused) — a piece is never the file now; if turning a note into MP3 fails on the server, the reason is written to the Activity log instead of staying invisible; and when the one key that can hear was resting, a key that cannot hear used to answer the note instead — a voice-note job now waits for a hearing key.
- Reactions: on the message, or not at all. Per the admin's word, a reaction that cannot land is never sent as a separate emoji text any more — it is dropped quietly, and the reason is in the Activity log as `reaction.not_landed`. The one-per-10-minutes rationing is gone, so the assistant reacts more often, and a reaction already on a message can be changed by reacting again.
